title: Linguistics, B.A. (College of the Liberal Arts)
notes: Built from the archived 2024-25 bulletin's 'Linguistics, B.A. at University Park Campus and Commonwealth Campuses' Suggested Academic Plan (a single combined plan that year -- UP and Commonwealth Campuses hadn't yet split into two separate suggested-plan tables, which only happens starting with the 2025-26 edition; see LING-2025.json/LING-2026.json) and its own Program Requirements course list. Verified the Program Requirements pool (Prescribed Courses LING 100/402/404/449 + Additional Courses: STAT 200 or appropriate statistics course, the 3-way LING 405/448/APLNG 200 pool, and the FR/GER/LATIN 450W/LING 493/SPAN multi-way 'Non-English Linguistics Course' pool, plus the two open-ended 6cr 400-level/related-field LING pools) is byte-identical to 2022's, 2023's, and 2026's -- same courses, same credit values, same 'Select one of the following' framing (this year's page drops the 'LATIN 450W History of Latin' title text down to just the bare code 'LATIN 450W', a change from 2022/2023's fully titled listing; GER 412 keeps its 2022/2023 title 'Contrastive Analysis of Modern German and English' this year and isn't retitled to 'Introduction to German linguistics' until the 2025-26 edition -- both are cosmetic title/description edits with no change to the pool itself; LATIN 450W is still excluded from this plan's modeled 'Non-English Linguistics Course' pool for the same reason as 2026: no latin_catalog.json exists in this repo yet). Real, confirmed differences from LING-2026.json's Suggested Academic Plan, same shape as LING-2022.json's and LING-2023.json's: (1) this year's plan has NO 'LA 283' / Second-Year Liberal Arts Seminar line item at all -- that requirement is new starting with the 2025-26 catalog edition, confirmed absent from 2022, 2023, and 2024's archived plans alike; dropping it removes the 3cr from Semester 1 and the 1.5cr line from Semester 4 that LING-2026.json models as fallback slots. (2) The itemized semester credits actually reconcile exactly to the bulletin's own stated 'Total Credits 120' this year (16+16+16+16+15+15+13.5+12.5=120) -- unlike LING-2026.json, which has a known, already-documented 3cr Semester-1 source-summarization gap (17.5 stated vs 14.5 itemized) caused by the newer LA 283 seminar's own bookkeeping; that gap simply doesn't exist in this cleaner, LA-283-free year. (3) Unlike 2022/2023, this year's bulletin already uses 'BA World Cultures Course' -- the same terminology LING-2026.json uses -- confirming the 'BA Other Cultures Course' -> 'BA World Cultures Course' rename happened for the 2024-25 catalog edition; modeled with the live terminology directly, no rename needed. (4) Elective placement differs slightly by semester (an Elective slot sits in Semester 1 here instead of Semester 4, since the LA 283 seminar that later displaces it doesn't exist yet) -- followed this year's own row-by-row table ordering rather than copying 2026's layout. Same real prereq-fix fallout as 2026, 2022, and 2023: the STAT 200 'Enforced Prerequisite at Enrollment: Placement into MATH 21 or higher' text was directly confirmed byte-identical between the archived 2022-23 STAT course-description page and the live 2026 STAT course-description page (see LING-2022.json's citation) with no signal of a mid-span change, so the same STAT 200/STAT 100 fallback modeling applies unchanged here without re-fetching this specific year's course-description page; the item resolves to STAT 100 (3cr instead of 4cr) rather than chasing the MATH 21/4/3 remedial placement chain this plan never otherwise schedules. Entrance to major requires a 2.00 GPA and third-semester classification, not modeled directly. Generic B.A. Field/Gen Ed/Elective pools modeled generically, matching the bulletin's own open-range phrasing, same convention as LING-2026.json. 'LING 4XX Course' (2 occurrences) and 'Related Area Course' (2 occurrences) remain generic -- this year's own bulletin phrasing is the same open-ended 'Select 6 additional credits in Linguistics at the 400 level' / 'Select 6 additional credits from Linguistics courses and/or approved related fields' with no further enumerated list.
